title: Availability cadence & SLO integration blueprint
body:
Purpose:
This blueprint defines a 90-day cross-functional project for formalizing availability cadence and integrating SLOs across product teams. Goal is a repeatable, low-friction workflow that ties SLOs -> telemetry -> error budget policy -> runbook actions and product rollouts. This is intentionally tactical: concrete owners, tickets, acceptance criteria and rehearsal plans.

Summary of approach:
- Focus on three exemplar services first (api-gateway, embed-service, console-ui) to validate the pattern.
- Pair eng-sre with each feature team for 6-week embedded collaboration.
- Instrumentation-first: ensure SLIs are reliable before locking SLO targets.
- Error budget automation: link to routing/fallback policies and release gates.

Key outcomes after 90 days:
1) SLO definitions for the three exemplar services with documented SLIs and measurement queries.
2) Dashboards and alert rules implemented in observability (dashboards + automated weekly error budget reports).
3) Error budget policy codified and integrated into CI/CD gating for canary rollouts.
4) Triage & escalation playbooks added to the team runbooks.
5) A lightweight onboarding kit for additional product teams to adopt the pattern.

High-level timeline (90 days):
- Week 0-2: Kickoff + discovery. Inventory SLIs, current dashboards, alert noise baseline. Run a 72-hour sampling of traffic and failures.
- Week 3-6: Instrumentation sprints. Owners implement missing telemetry, fix cardinality issues, and stabilize query performance.
- Week 7-10: SLO design sessions. Set SLO targets, error budget burn models, and acceptance tests.
- Week 11-13: Automation & rollout. Wire error budget checks into canary gate, create dashboards, schedule weekly reports.
- Week 14: Rehearse tabletop incident using new playbooks. Retrospective and adoption plan.

Stakeholders & roles:
- Project lead: Maya Chen (eng-sre) — program coordination, blockers, exec updates.
- SRE partners: Ethan Brooks, Zoe Patel — runbook authors, alert tuning.
- Product leads: Priya Nair (Hosted API), Lucas Martín (Dedicated) — define customer impact and SLA constraints.
- Observability owner: Daniel O. (platform-observability) — dashboards, metric schema.
- Release engineer: Anya V. (release-engineering) — integrate error-budget checks into release pipelines.
- Security/compliance reviewer: Samir K. — ensure telemetry and logs respect PII/KMS rules.

Work items (high priority, ticket examples):
- ENG-1427: SLI inventory & baseline report (owner: Maya) — deliverable: CSV of metrics and heatmap.
- ENG-1482: api-gateway request-latency SLI instrumentation (owner: Ethan) — deliverable: histogram + percentile query.
- OBS-334: dashboard templates for SLO coverage (owner: Daniel) — deliverable: templated dashboards + widgets.
- REL-221: canary gate integration for error budget (owner: Anya) — deliverable: pipeline check + rollback hook.
- RUN-019: runbook drafts and tabletop scenario (owner: Zoe) — deliverable: runbook pages + scenario notes.

SLO/SLI definitions (example pattern):
- SLI: successful_response_rate (30s window) = 1 - (rate(5xx OR timeout) / total_requests)
- SLO: successful_response_rate >= 99.5% (monthly) for customer-facing critical routes
- Measurement notes: use high-cardinality sampling for per-route SLIs, aggregate to service-level for alerting.

Error budget policy (proposal):
- Burn window: 7-day sliding for operational alerts, monthly for release gating.
- Burn thresholds and actions:
  - Burn > 0% and < 25%: platform notify (weekly email), no gating changes.
  - Burn >= 25% and < 60%: pause non-critical feature rollouts; SRE deep-dive; increase oncall staffing.
  - Burn >= 60%: emergency rollback candidate; escalate to SRE lead + Product; disable experimental routes.
- Auto-remediation: for specific well-understood failures (e.g., circuit-breaker tripped), trigger an automated scaling operation; otherwise require human sign-off.

Acceptance criteria for an exemplar service to be "SLO-ready":
- All SLIs computed from production telemetry for 30 days with < 1% query error rate.
- Dashboard shows error budget remaining and burn rate.
- Canary pipeline has automated gate using error budget metric.
- Runbook includes RCA checklist and at least one automated remediation path.
- Product team has signed the SLO doc and understands rollback triggers.

Telemetry & instrumentation checklist:
- Confirm metrics use stable metric names and labels (per tagging policy).
- Ensure cardinality limits applied to high-cardinality labels and sample where necessary.
- Export histograms for latency with consistent buckets.
- Add synthetic transactions for critical user journeys (console login, embed request).
- Create sum/count metrics for success/failure classification.

Communication plan:
- Weekly SLO sync (30m) with product/SRE partners on Thursdays 11:00 PST.
- Error budget digest (automated) email every Monday with top 3 services by burn.
- Slack: #sre-slo-adoption (alerts, questions, quick escalations).
- Executive cadence: bi-weekly exec summary in Reliability OKR update.

Risk register (top risks + mitigation):
- Risk: Telemetry gaps -> false SLO measurements. Mitigation: instrumentation sprints first, sampling audit (ENG-1427).
- Risk: Alert fatigue from poorly tuned rules. Mitigation: quiet-hours, alert-runbook mapping, SRE-led tuning slots.
- Risk: Release pipeline complexity blocking adoption. Mitigation: build a minimal gate first (read-only checks) then expand to blocking gates.
- Risk: Ownership ambiguity. Mitigation: add explicit SLO steward per service and update team charters.

Operational rehearsal plan (tabletop):
- Scenario: Sudden 40% error-rate increase for embed-service during peak.
- Participants: product owner, SRE oncall, release engineer, support lead.
- Steps: detect (dashboard), runbook guided triage, decision (route traffic fallback), execute rollback if error budget > 60%.
- Postmortem: 48-hour writeback with action owners and timelines.

Onboarding kit (deliverables to replicate pattern):
- SLO template (doc) with example queries and SLI measurement guidance.
- Dashboard JSON templates for the observability platform.
- Runbook skeleton with incident checklist and error budget actions.
- Checklist to add gating to CI/CD (minimal YAML snippet).

Metrics to track program success (KPIs):
- Percent of critical services with defined SLOs (target: 60% by day 90).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO breaches.
- Time-to-code for instrumentation fixes (median days).
- Number of rollbacks prevented by early error budget signals.
- Team adoption score (survey after week 12).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Kickoff meeting: schedule with product leads and observers; share discovery template (owner: Maya, ticket ENG-1427).
2) Run instrumentation sprint for api-gateway (owner: Ethan, ticket ENG-1482).
3) Observability team to prepare dashboard templates (owner: Daniel, ticket OBS-334).
4) Release leads to prototype a read-only error budget check in a canary pipeline (owner: Anya, ticket REL-221).

Notes & open questions:
- What is the canonical owner for global SLO policy (SRE org or platform product)? Need decision by Week 2.
- Are there regulatory constraints for synthetic transactions in EU regions? Security to confirm.
- Should we adopt the same monthly SLO window for all services or allow per-service windows? Recommendation: use monthly default with exceptions documented.

Appendix: quick reference links
- Confluence SLO registry: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/SLO+Registry
- Initial tickets: ENG-1427, ENG-1482, OBS-334, REL-221
- Slack: #sre-slo-adoption
